course.title: Russian A1 · Pareto-first survival path
course.design: Prioritize a small high-leverage core, then expand breadth through repeated meaningful use.

paretoTiers.label: Survival core
paretoTiers.description: The smallest high-leverage set for introductions, repair, questions, needs, time, food, places, and basic navigation.
paretoTiers.targetBehavior: Prioritize in first exposure, daily sessions, adaptive review, and checkpoint recovery.

paretoTiers.label: High-frequency A1 core
paretoTiers.description: Common words and chunks that unlock most recurring beginner interactions after the survival layer.
paretoTiers.targetBehavior: Recycle across multiple units and modalities before adding supporting breadth.

paretoTiers.label: Supporting breadth
paretoTiers.description: Lower-frequency or contextual material that adds flexibility after the core is stable.
paretoTiers.targetBehavior: Introduce when core performance and learner capacity support it.

u03-numbers-time.title: Numbers, dates, and time
u03-numbers-time.objective: Ask and answer simple questions about numbers, days, dates, and the time of a meeting.

activities.title: Wake up the core
activities.prompt: Say today, tomorrow, and now before learning new numbers.

activities.title: Meet the time words
activities.prompt: Connect each Russian word to a useful beginner meaning.

activities.title: Listen for the number
activities.prompt: Hear the phrase, notice the stressed syllable, then repeat it aloud.

activities.title: Build a simple answer
activities.prompt: Answer «Который час?» with a time, then answer «Во сколько?» with в + time.

activities.title: Use it in a plan
activities.prompt: Complete the short dialogue and understand the tiny story.

patterns.en: What time is it? — It is three o’clock now.

patterns.ru: Во сколько встречаемся? — В три часа.
patterns.en: What time shall we meet? — At three o’clock.
patterns.pron: vo SKOL-ka fstre-CHA-yem-sya? — f tree cha-SA

grammar.title: Который час? vs Во сколько?
grammar.explanation: Use «Который час?» to ask the current time. Use «Во сколько?» to ask when an event happens. A simple answer uses «В» plus the time: «В три часа».
grammar.exampleRu: Во сколько встречаемся? — В три часа.
grammar.exampleEn: What time shall we meet? — At three o’clock.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not use the current-time question when you mean the time of an appointment.

turns.prompt: Say that it is three o’clock.
Say that you will meet at three.
Understand the closing.

lines.ru: Сегодня понедельник.
lines.en: Today is Monday.

lines.ru: Сейчас три часа.
lines.en: It is three o’clock now.

lines.ru: Завтра я работаю утром.
lines.en: Tomorrow I work in the morning.

lines.ru: Вечером мы встречаемся.
lines.en: In the evening we meet.

questions.prompt: Choose the phrase for “tomorrow”.
Choose the natural answer to «Во сколько?».
Choose the phrase for “What time is it?”.

checkpoint.completionRule: Answer at least 2 of 3 correctly and complete both dialogue turns.

u02-greetings-introductions.title: Greetings and introductions
u02-greetings-introductions.objective: Greet someone, exchange names, and say where you are from in a short Russian conversation.

activities.title: Open the conversation
activities.prompt: Choose a greeting that fits the situation.

activities.title: Build your introduction
activities.prompt: Connect names and origins to useful meanings.

activities.title: Notice the question
activities.prompt: Hear the difference between informal and formal name questions.

activities.title: Say who you are

activities.title: Meet someone new
activities.prompt: Complete the dialogue and follow the short story.

patterns.en: Where are you from? — I am from Canada.

grammar.title: Ты vs Вы
grammar.explanation: Use «ты» with friends and people your age when the situation is informal. Use «вы» for a stranger, an older person, or a polite interaction. «Как вас зовут?» is the safe formal question.
grammar.exampleRu: Как вас зовут? — Меня зовут Анна.
grammar.exampleEn: What is your name? — My name is Anna.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not switch to «ты» with a stranger before the situation becomes informal.

turns.prompt: Say your name politely.
Say where you are from.
Understand the closing.

lines.ru: Здравствуйте! Меня зовут Ольга.
lines.en: Hello! My name is Olga.

lines.ru: Я из Москвы.
lines.en: I am from Moscow.

lines.ru: Это мой новый друг Марк.
lines.en: This is my new friend Mark.

lines.ru: Очень приятно!
lines.en: Nice to meet you!

questions.prompt: Choose the polite greeting.

u04-people-family.title: People and family
u04-people-family.objective: Describe the important people around you and ask who someone is using simple Russian sentences.

activities.title: Name the people
activities.prompt: Retrieve the family and friend words you need most.

activities.title: Meet the people
activities.prompt: Connect people words to their meanings and genders.

activities.title: Hear who it is
activities.prompt: Notice the difference between «он» and «она».

activities.title: Describe your family
activities.prompt: Build a sentence with мой, моя, он, or она.

activities.title: Introduce someone
activities.prompt: Complete the dialogue and understand the family story.

patterns.en: Who is this? — This is my brother.

patterns.ru: Он мой друг. Она моя подруга.
patterns.en: He is my friend. She is my friend.
patterns.pron: on moy drook. a-NA ma-YA pa-DOO-ga

grammar.title: Мой or моя? Он or она?
grammar.explanation: Use «мой» with a masculine noun such as брат or друг, and «моя» with a feminine noun such as сестра or подруга. Use «он» for he and «она» for she.
grammar.exampleRu: Это моя сестра. Она моя подруга.
grammar.exampleEn: This is my sister. She is my friend.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not use «мой» before a feminine noun: say «моя сестра».

turns.prompt: Say that this is your sister.
Say that this is your brother.
Understand the closing.

lines.ru: Это моя семья.
lines.en: This is my family.

lines.ru: Это мой брат Илья.
lines.en: This is my brother Ilya.

lines.ru: А это моя сестра Нина.
lines.en: And this is my sister Nina.

lines.ru: Мы вместе дома.
lines.en: We are together at home.

checkpoint.title: People check

questions.prompt: Choose the correct phrase for “my sister”.
Choose the phrase for “Who is this?”.
Choose the correct pronoun for Нина.

u05-home-objects.title: Home and everyday objects
u05-home-objects.objective: Talk about what is at home while reusing greetings, family, time, and meeting phrases in one connected beginner conversation.

activities.prompt: Bring greetings, family words, and time phrases back before adding home words.

activities.prompt: Complete the recycled dialogue, story, and cumulative checkpoint.

patterns.en: The book is on the table.

grammar.title: Где? — дома, здесь, там
grammar.explanation: Use «дома» for being at home, «здесь» for here, and «там» for there. The phrase «в три часа» keeps the appointment pattern from Unit 3 active.
grammar.exampleRu: Сегодня мы дома. Приходи в три часа.
grammar.exampleEn: Today we are at home. Come over at three o’clock.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not answer «Где?» with «дом» when you mean location; use «дома».

turns.prompt: Say that you are at home.
Invite your friend for three o’clock.
Understand the closing.

lines.en: Hello! Today we are at home.

lines.ru: Моя сестра пьёт чай.
lines.en: My sister is drinking tea.

lines.ru: Книга на столе.
lines.en: The book is on the table.

lines.ru: Марк приходит в три часа.
lines.en: Mark is coming at three o’clock.

u06-food-cafe.title: Food and café
u06-food-cafe.objective: Order simple food and drinks, ask the price, and complete a polite café transaction while recycling the core conversation patterns.

patterns.en: How much does the coffee cost?

grammar.title: Polite requests with пожалуйста
grammar.explanation: Use «пожалуйста» to soften a request: «Дайте, пожалуйста, чай» or «Счёт, пожалуйста». Russian café requests can be short and direct while still polite.
grammar.exampleEn: Coffee, please. How much does it cost?
grammar.commonMistake: Do not omit «пожалуйста» when making a short request to a server or cashier.

turns.prompt: Order tea politely.
Ask how much the coffee costs.

turns.en: That will be three hundred rubles.
turns.prompt: Understand the transaction closing.

lines.ru: Здравствуйте! Мы встречаемся в кафе.

lines.ru: Моя сестра хочет чай, а я хочу кофе.
lines.en: My sister wants tea, and I want coffee.

lines.ru: Дайте, пожалуйста, суп и хлеб.

u07-shopping-clothing.title: Travel, directions, and transportation
u07-shopping-clothing.objective: Ask where a place is, understand a simple route, and use public transportation while recycling the A1 conversation core.

activities.title: Plan the trip
activities.prompt: Bring greetings, time, family, home, food, and price language into one travel situation.

activities.prompt: Connect the most useful direction and transport words to their meanings.

activities.title: Reach the café
activities.prompt: Complete the travel dialogue, recycled listening, and cumulative checkpoint.

patterns.en: How do I get to the café?

grammar.title: Route chunks: до, на, и потом
grammar.explanation: Use memorized route chunks such as «до кафе» for to the café, «на метро» for by metro, and «потом» for then. These short chunks make directions easier to understand before studying every case ending.
grammar.exampleRu: Идите прямо, потом направо. Кафе рядом.
grammar.exampleEn: Go straight, then right. The café is nearby.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not translate “by metro” as «в метро» when you mean the transport you take; use «на метро».

turns.en: Excuse me, where is the metro station?
turns.prompt: Ask how to get to the café.
Say that you need a ticket.
Understand the route closing.

lines.ru: Здравствуйте! Сегодня мы едем в город.
lines.en: Hello! Today we are going to the city.

lines.ru: Моя сестра спрашивает: «Где станция метро?»
lines.en: My sister asks: “Where is the metro station?”

lines.ru: Идите прямо, потом налево.
lines.en: Go straight, then left.

lines.ru: Мы покупаем билет и едем в кафе.
lines.en: We buy a ticket and go to the café.

lines.ru: Вечером мы вместе дома.
lines.en: In the evening we are together at home.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Кафе рядом» — what does that tell you?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This recycles the place word from the home unit.

u08-daily-routine.title: Hotel check-in, accommodation, and emergency help
u08-daily-routine.objective: Check into a hotel, report a room problem, and ask for urgent help while staying calm and clear.

activities.title: Arrive safely
activities.prompt: Bring greetings, travel, tickets, café, home, and time phrases into a hotel arrival.

activities.title: Check in
activities.prompt: Connect the most useful hotel, room, and emergency words to their meanings.

activities.title: Hear the problem
activities.prompt: Listen for the room issue, location, and urgent request in short help phrases.

activities.title: Report clearly
activities.prompt: Say where you are, what is wrong, and what help you need.

activities.title: Solve the stay
activities.prompt: Complete the hotel dialogue, recycled listening, and cumulative checkpoint.

patterns.en: I have a problem in the room.

grammar.title: У меня есть / у меня проблема
grammar.explanation: Use «У меня есть…» to present what you have, and «У меня проблема…» to report a problem. Match descriptive words to feminine room nouns: «горячая вода» and «холодная вода».
grammar.exampleRu: У меня проблема в номере. Горячая вода не работает.
grammar.exampleEn: I have a problem in the room. The hot water does not work.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not use the emergency phrase «Помогите!» as a casual request; reserve it for urgent danger or immediate need.

dialogue.title: Checking in and reporting a room problem

turns.prompt: Say that you have a reservation.
Report that the shower does not work.
Say that you need help in an urgent situation.

lines.ru: Здравствуйте! У меня есть бронирование.

lines.ru: Моя сестра показывает паспорт.
lines.en: My sister shows her passport.

lines.en: In the evening we are together in a nearby café.

u09-work-school.title: Work, school, and languages
u09-work-school.objective: Talk simply about work, school, languages, ability, and communication repair.

activities.title: Meet after work
activities.prompt: Bring greetings, time, travel, café, hotel, and help phrases into a work or study conversation.

activities.title: Work and study
activities.prompt: Connect the most useful work, school, and language words to their meanings.

activities.title: Catch the language
activities.prompt: Listen for workplaces, study locations, languages, and repair requests.

activities.prompt: Complete the language-meetup dialogue, recycled listening, and cumulative checkpoint.

patterns.ru: Я говорю по-английски и немного по-русски.
patterns.en: I speak English and a little Russian.
patterns.pron: ya ga-va-RYOO pa-ang-LEE-skee ee nee-MNO-ga pa-ROOS-kee

patterns.en: I do not understand. Please repeat.

grammar.title: Present-tense work, study, and language frames
grammar.explanation: Use first-person forms such as «я работаю», «я учусь», «я говорю», and «я понимаю». Use «по-русски» and «по-английски» to say which language you speak.
grammar.exampleRu: Я немного говорю по-русски, но не всё понимаю.
grammar.exampleEn: I speak a little Russian, but I do not understand everything.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not translate “in Russian” as «в русский» here. For speaking a language, use «по-русски».

turns.prompt: Say that you work in an office.
Say that you speak a little Russian.

turns.en: Of course. If you do not understand, say so.
turns.prompt: Ask the person to speak more slowly.

lines.ru: После работы я иду в университет.

lines.ru: Моя сестра учится там, а я изучаю русский язык.
lines.en: My sister studies there, and I study Russian.

lines.ru: В шесть часов у нас урок.

lines.en: I speak a little Russian, but I do not understand everything.

lines.en: The teacher speaks more slowly and helps me.

recycling.title: Cumulative work-and-language loop
recycling.summary: This unit reuses practical arrival, place, time, café, and repair language while adding work, study, and language ability. The learner practices keeping a conversation going even when comprehension is incomplete.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Я работаю в офисе» — where does the speaker work?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This is a high-frequency workplace frame.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Я учусь в университете» — what does the speaker do?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This recycles place language and adds study.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Я немного говорю по-русски» — how well does the speaker speak Russian?
listeningContrasts.explanation: «Немного» is a useful honest ability qualifier.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Повторите, пожалуйста» — what is the speaker asking for?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This keeps a conversation moving without pretending to understand.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «Говорите медленнее» — how should the other person speak?
listeningContrasts.explanation: This is a practical listening-repair request.

listeningContrasts.prompt: You hear «В шесть часов у нас урок» — what happens at six?
listeningContrasts.hear: В шесть часов у нас урок.
listeningContrasts.explanation: This combines Unit 3 time with the new study context.

u10-city-directions.objective: Ask for places in the city, understand simple directions, and reach a destination by walking or transport.

grammar.title: Weather with холодно, жарко, and будет
grammar.explanation: Russian often describes weather with an impersonal word: «холодно», «жарко», «тепло». Use «сегодня» for today and «завтра будет…» for a simple tomorrow forecast.
grammar.exampleRu: Сегодня холодно, а завтра будет тепло. Возьмите куртку.

grammar.title: Chunk stacking for survival communication
grammar.explanation: In a stressful situation, stack short reliable chunks: «Извините» + question, «У меня проблема» + need, or «Повторите…» + repair request. Clear chunks are more useful than long sentences.
grammar.exampleRu: Извините. У меня проблема. Мне нужна помощь, пожалуйста.
grammar.exampleEn: Excuse me. I have a problem. I need help, please.
grammar.commonMistake: Do not stop after «Я не понимаю». Add «Повторите, пожалуйста, медленнее» or show the relevant place, object, or need.

lines.ru: Сегодня Анна приезжает в новый город.
lines.en: Today Anna arrives in a new city.

lines.ru: Она спрашивает: «Извините, где находится вокзал?»
lines.en: She asks: “Excuse me, where is the station?”

lines.ru: Потом у неё проблема с билетом, но она просит повторить медленнее.
lines.en: Then she has a problem with the ticket, but she asks for it to be repeated more slowly.

lines.ru: После этого она находит гостиницу и аптеку рядом.
lines.en: After that she finds the hotel and pharmacy nearby.

lines.ru: Вечером она говорит: «Спасибо за помощь» и строит план на завтра.
lines.en: In the evening she says: “Thanks for the help” and makes a plan for tomorrow.

recycling.title: Complete A1 survival loop
recycling.summary: The capstone combines all prior themes into one practical mission: arrive, find places, handle a ticket or health issue, repair communication, thank someone, and plan tomorrow.
